specification_sets.label: GU81 swimming / wading / waterslide pool — chlorine, water temperature 26 °C or below
specification_sets.applies_to: Public swimming pools, wading pools and waterslides disinfected with chlorine, pool water temperature ≤ 26 °C. NOTE: the '≤' glyph is not recoverable from the PDF text layer — the cell extracts as a blank followed by '26OC' and is paired in the same table with a '> 26OC' row, so '≤' is the only consistent reading. Confirm against the printed page.
specification_sets.source_section: 4-16 Water Quality Requirements, Table 5: Pool Water Standard Quality Parameters

limits.source_quote: Table 5 row 'Chlorine | ≤26OC | 7.2 - 7.6 | 60 - 200 mg/l2 | Min. 1 - 2 mg/l3 | 30 - 50 mg/l'. The endpoints carry NO operator glyph; read as inclusive because the body text at 4-16 requires the value be 'continuously controlled and monitored within the ranges as specified in Table 5'.

Table 5 cell '60 - 200 mg/l2'. Footnote 2: 'If disinfectant used is gaseous chlorine the total alkalinity should range from 150 to 200 mg/l.' — that narrower range applies ONLY where the disinfectant is gaseous chlorine and is not encoded here. Endpoints carry no operator glyph; read as inclusive per the 'within the ranges' wording at 4-16.

Table 5 cell 'Min. 1 - 2 mg/l3'. The minimum is CONDITIONAL, per footnote 3 (p31): 'If cyanuric acid is used, minimum free chlorine is 2 mg/l at ≤26OC and 4 mg/l at > 26OC. For unstabilized pool water (without cyanuric acid), minimum free chlorine is 1 mg/l at ≤26OC and 2 mg/l at > 26OC.' min_val is therefore set to the LOWEST value the document permits in this band (1 mg/l, unstabilized water); a stabilized pool is actually held to 2 mg/l and this limit will under-detect that case. Upper bound from footnote 7 (p31): 'The maximum level for both free chlorine and bromine shall not exceed 10 mg/l.' — 'shall not exceed' is inclusive. Requires human resolution into stabilized / unstabilized sets before sale.

Table 5 cell '30 - 50 mg/l' under the 'Cyanuric Acid1' column. Footnote 1 (p31): 'Stabilizer (cyanuric acid and chlorinated cyanurates) is not allowed to be used in indoor pools (swimming pool, wading pool, or waterslide) which includes spa pool and hydrotherapy pool (both indoor and outdoor).' This limit therefore applies to OUTDOOR pools only. Endpoints carry no operator glyph.

Table 5 cell '60 - 200 mg/l2'. Footnote 2 narrows to 150 - 200 mg/l for gaseous chlorine only; not encoded here.

Table 5 cell 'Min. 2 - 3 mg/l3'. NOTE A DOCUMENT INCONSISTENCY: footnote 3 gives only two temperature bands — 'minimum free chlorine is 2 mg/l at ≤26OC and 4 mg/l at > 26OC' (stabilized) and '1 mg/l at ≤26OC and 2 mg/l at > 26OC' (unstabilized) — which yields {2, 4} for this band, not the '2 - 3' printed in the table cell. min_val is set to the lowest value either source permits (2 mg/l). Upper bound from footnote 7: 'The maximum level for both free chlorine and bromine shall not exceed 10 mg/l.' Must be resolved with DM before this set is sold.
Table 5 cell '30 - 50 mg/l'. Footnote 1 restricts stabilizer use to outdoor pools, so this limit applies to outdoor pools only.

specification_sets.label: GU81 swimming / wading / waterslide pool — bromine, water temperature 26 °C or below
specification_sets.applies_to: Public swimming pools, wading pools and waterslides disinfected with bromine, pool water temperature ≤ 26 °C ('≤' glyph not recoverable from the text layer — see gu81_pool_chlorine_le26).
specification_sets.source_section: 4-16 Water Quality Requirements, Table 5: Pool Water Standard Quality Parameters

limits.source_quote: Table 5 bromine sub-row '≤26OC | 7.2 - 7.8 | 60 - 200 mg/l4 | 2 mg/l'. Endpoints carry no operator glyph; read as inclusive per 'within the ranges' at 4-16.

Table 5 cell '60 - 200 mg/l4'. Footnote 4: 'If disinfectant used is 1-Bromo-3-chloro-5, 5-dimethylhydantoin (BCDMH) the total alkalinity should range from 150 to 200 mg/l.' — narrower BCDMH range not encoded here.

Table 5 cell reads exactly '2 mg/l' with NO operator and NO 'Min.' prefix — unlike every chlorine cell in the same table and unlike the hydrotherapy and spa bromine cells, which read 'Min. 4 mg/l' and 'Min. 8 mg/l'. Whether 2 mg/l is a floor, a target or a ceiling is therefore NOT stated for this row, so min_inclusive is left null rather than guessed; min_val 2.0 is recorded on the parallel with the 'Min.' rows but must be confirmed. Upper bound is firm — footnote 7: 'The maximum level for both free chlorine and bromine shall not exceed 10 mg/l.'

specification_sets.label: GU81 all pool types — calcium hardness and saturation index
specification_sets.applies_to: All types of public pool, whether indoor or outdoor (footnote 9 states this explicitly).

limits.source_quote: Footnote 9: 'Calcium Hardness shall be between 100 to 500 mg/l and Saturation Index shall be between -0.5 to 0.5. These parameter values are applicable to all types of pools whether indoor and outdoor.' 'between X to Y' carries no operator glyph; read as inclusive.

Footnote 9: 'Calcium Hardness shall be between 100 to 500 mg/l and Saturation Index shall be between -0.5 to 0.5. These parameter values are applicable to all types of pools whether indoor and outdoor.' No operator glyph; read as inclusive.

specification_sets.label: GU81 pool water — microbiological parameters (all pool types)
specification_sets.applies_to: All public swimming pool water covered by GU81. Table 6 is not qualified by pool type or disinfectant.
specification_sets.source_section: 4-16 Water Quality Requirements, Table 6: Maximum Allowable Microbiological Parameters

limits.source_quote: Table 6 'Maximum Allowable Microbiological Parameters': 'Total Coliforms | 0 mpn/100 ml.' A stated acceptable range of zero under a 'Maximum Allowable' heading means any detection breaches; qualifier_rule is detect_fails so a laboratory's 'Absent' / 'Not Detected' / '<1' passes and any quantified value fails, rather than a non-detect being coerced to a measured zero.
Table 6 (continued onto p32): 'Fecal Coliforms | 0 mpn/100 ml.'

Table 6: 'Heterotrophic Plate Count | 1000 cfu/ml.' The cell carries no operator glyph; inclusivity is taken from the table heading 'Maximum Allowable Microbiological Parameters', under which 1000 is itself allowable. CAUTION: this PDF is known to drop '≤' glyphs (see the temperature cells in Table 5), so the cell may read '≤ 1000' on the printed page — which would give the same inclusive reading.
Table 6: 'Pseudomonas Aeruginosa | 0 cfu/100 ml.'
Table 6: 'Fecal Streptococci | 0 cfu/100 ml.'

obligations.cadence_note: Document states an explicit daily cadence: 'tested daily (before use)'. Encoded as cadence_days 1. Note the cadence is tied to USE — a pool closed for a period has no reading due — which cadence_days alone cannot express.
obligations.applies_to: Public swimming pool water — pH, chlorine and temperature. Tested before use each day; readings recorded in a logbook.
obligations.source_quote: p30, 4-16: 'Water quality shall be tested daily (before use) for pH, chlorine, and temperature levels.' and 'All readings shall be recorded in a logbook.'

obligations.cadence_note: Document states an explicit cadence: 'for every 15 days'. Encoded as cadence_days 15 rather than a half-month, because the document counts in days.
obligations.applies_to: Public swimming pool water — calcium hardness, alkalinity, saturation index and cyanuric acid.
obligations.source_quote: p30, 4-16: 'Pool water shall also be tested for calcium hardness, alkalinity, saturation index and cyanuric acid for every 15 days. All readings shall be recorded in a logbook.'

obligations.cadence_note: Document states an explicit cadence: 'every two months'. Encoded as cadence_months 2. No grace period is stated anywhere in GU81.
obligations.applies_to: Public swimming pool water — microbiological parameters (Table 6: total coliforms, fecal coliforms, heterotrophic plate count, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, fecal streptococci). This is the laboratory-evidenced obligation.
obligations.source_quote: p30, 4-16: 'Pool water shall be tested for microbiological parameters every two months.'
